intended_object: The functor C ⥤ CosimplicialObject C that sends an object X to the constant cosimplicial object at X: every [n] goes to X and every map goes to the identity. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
`CosimplicialObject C` is by definition `SimplexCategory ⥤ C`. The body is `Functor.const SimplexCategory`, the standard constant-diagram functor C ⥤ (J ⥤ C) taken at J = SimplexCategory. It sends X to the functor that is constantly X, with identity maps, and sends a morphism f to the natural transformation whose every component is f. That is exactly the constant cosimplicial object construction.

This is a convenience abbreviation of the general Mathlib construction `Functor.const`, not a reimplementation of it. It is the cosimplicial counterpart of `SimplicialObject.const`. Specializing to the simplex category is the whole point of the notion, so it is not too narrow.
